newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government to sell Thomson to Lagardere.
newsitem.headline: French government to sell Thomson to Lagardere.

text.p: The French government said on Wednesday it planned to transfer state-owned electronics group Thomson SA to books-to-missiles conglomerate Lagardere Groupe.
The government said it was giving both the offers from Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom to the Privatisation Commission but added it had a preference for Lagardere.
The government said it would recapitalise Thomson SA for 11 billion francs ($2.1 billion), taken from the state's privatisation receipts.
The government said it had taken its decision because of the synergies of a merger between Lagardere's Matra defence unit and Thomson-CSF, in which Thomson SA has a 58 percent stake.
The state will keep a special share in Thomson SA out of national security reasons.
It said Lagardere aimed to leave the share capital of semiconductor maker SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV, in which Thomson-CSF has a 20 percent stake.
The government said Lagardere had arranged for Korea's Daewoo Electronics to take control of Thomson Multimedia.
The Paris Bourse delayed the opening of shares in Alcatel, Lagardere and Thomson-CSF ($ = 5.213 French Francs)
